Gabriella, we are sorry to see that your perception of our service changed. During the time we cared for your pet, your experiences with our team were consistently positive. Unfortunately, the situation changed after a phone conversation regarding the doctor’s recommendation to have her re-evaluated before prescribing additional medication.
We understand that a medical recommendation may not always be what a pet owner expects. However, our responsibility is to prioritize the health and safety of our patients and to follow the doctor’s medical judgment. We also expect our team to be treated with the same professionalism and respect that we extend to every client.
We regret that the situation ended on a different note than how our relationship with your family began. We wish you and your pet all the best moving forward.

My cat was the first one in the morning but the last one out, even though he hadn't eaten since the previous afternoon. It turns out the vet has a very rude man working at reception who wouldn't even let me stay inside the clinic when it was already 5 p.m. and I went to see what was happening with my cat. I argued with this man and left the clinic because of all the insults he hurled at me. I wouldn't have stopped taking my cat to the vet, but customer service is incredibly important, and I also felt that my cat was discriminated against that day.

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!! Best service at very reasonable prices. And the actual Veterinarian examines and treats your pet. In Miami-Dade, in many vet offices, 90% of the care is done by the techs, not the Vet. Nothing against techs but in that lopsided business model, the vet never gets to really know your pet. They rely on the tech for almost everything. Imagine a nurse, even a great one, telling your doctor, its cancer and the doctor says, OK lets operate. Crazy right? At Miami Pet Clinic, they have great techs, believe me. But the actual doctor examines your pet alongside them and that real time communication can make all the difference for your loved one. And the cost for that examination is extremely reasonable compared to many vet offices in the area.

I brought my two cats to Miami Pet Clinic with high expectations for a routine wellness check and vaccinations. Unfortunately, the experience didn’t live up to that.

There were a few minor issues that were frustrating, though not deal-breakers on their own. For example, I had already created detailed profiles for both cats in their PetDesk app, including diet and general info, yet I still had to fill out paperwork upon arrival and then repeat the same information again during the appointment. It felt redundant and outdated, especially for a clinic using a digital platform.

The main issue, however, was how they handle cats with behavioral challenges. One of my cats is not friendly with strangers and requires proper handling (like using a towel or wrap). After asking about this, I was told they don’t handle pets that can’t be examined freely. That was surprising and honestly disappointing, this is a veterinary clinic, and not all pets are going to be easy.

If your cat is even slightly difficult or anxious, this may not be the right place, you could end up wasting your time.

The only positive was that they refunded my deposit. That said, there was no apology or acknowledgment of the inconvenience, which didn’t sit well.

Overall, not a good fit if your cat isn’t naturally cooperative.

You only need to read the 1-star reviews to realize that they're not only negligent but also not a serious or responsible veterinary clinic. The review is below. Basically, we adopted a stray cat, took her to them, and asked them to check absolutely everything: diseases, pregnancy, deworming, etc. Logically, if you take in a stray cat, you'd think they'd triple-check everything. It's ridiculous that they wash their hands of it, saying she was pregnant but we didn't notice. Now, the first time, okay, fine, you didn't notice because of your negligence, since all that matters here is the money. But we went back weeks later, and they still hadn't noticed! It's impossible that a vet wouldn't have any better tools to detect a pregnancy than "their hands," haha. And the most unbelievable thing is that we took her back a week before she was due to give birth, worried because she looked quite chubby, and their response was to give her less food. They have neither logic nor common sense, and frankly, I'm not surprised. If I can tell you anything, look elsewhere or read the bad reviews. Basically, if I take my pet for a checkup and you don't notice, is that my responsibility? Then why am I paying? Are things going to be tested in 2026 based on whether I notice or not? CLOWNS

Rabies vaccination was properly administered, but the guidance provided regarding international travel and U.S. re-entry requirements was incomplete.

I specifically scheduled this appointment to ensure my dog would be able to re-enter the United States from a rabies high-risk country such as Brazil without complications, during a known CDC regulatory transition period. I clearly remember asking whether the documentation I was given at the appointment would be sufficient for future U.S. re-entry, and I was told that it would be.

This visit took place just a few days before July 31, the deadline related to the transition period for submitting U.S. rabies documentation, so this was not an unexpected or unknown regulatory change at the time.

What was particularly frustrating is that responsibility was later placed on me for “leaving the U.S. without the proper documents,” when my dog traveled from the U.S. to Spain — a destination that does not require a USDA Export Health Certificate. Therefore, there was no missing document to issue at that point.

While the medical care itself was fine and staff was polite, clearer and more proactive counseling for international pet travel cases would have prevented significant stress and logistical issues.

I am updating my review to provide additional context and clarity, as the clinic’s response does not fully reflect my experience or the reasons for my dissatisfaction.

The following reflects my personal experience as a client, based on events as they occurred and my perception of how they were handled.

I have taken both of my pets, Bella and Marley, to this clinic on separate occasions. My concerns do not stem from a single interaction but from a pattern of experiences that, in my opinion, reveal shortcomings in communication, client care, and empathy.

Bella was brought in for soft stools. During that visit, I was informed of several findings, including kidney concerns, heart issues, anemia, and periodontal disease. The way this information was presented led me to believe her condition was hopeless rather than manageable.

I recall being called to have Bella tested again due to suspected kidney problems, which proved unfounded. I informed them she was eating and urinating normally and, although unwell, had not lost her appetite. She was diagnosed with a stomach infection, and treatment was limited to medication to stop vomiting and iron for anemia caused by it.

Seeking clarity, I obtained a second opinion. That evaluation indicated her kidney and heart function were consistent with her age (almost 19 years), no treatment was necessary at that time, and she was not in critical or end-of-life condition. This stark contrast affected my confidence and raised concerns about how the original medical information was communicated.

Regarding Marley, I made a good-faith effort to provide complete and accurate information beforehand. I called prior to the appointment, disclosed his diagnosed heart condition, confirmed he was on daily medication, and offered to email his medical records in advance. I was instructed instead to bring printed copies.

On the appointment day, I arrived around 9 a.m., following the clinic’s fasting instructions. Marley had not eaten since 9 p.m. the previous night, and as a direct result, I withheld his morning heart medication.

After Marley’s exam and record review, approximately two hours passed without proactive communication from the clinic, despite my multiple calls seeking updates. Around 11 a.m., I was informed the procedure would not proceed and that additional diagnostic testing was needed to assess anesthesia risk.

I fully understand and respect the need for caution with anesthesia in cardiac patients. My concern is not the medical decision itself but the delay in communication and how the situation was managed, especially given Marley’s known condition, prolonged fasting, withheld medication, and increased stress.

Statements suggesting a short fasting period would not cause harm miss the core issue. The problem, from my perspective, is the lack of timely communication, anticipation, and empathy under known circumstances.

**Communication, Fees, and Client Experience**

When scheduling the appointment, payment instructions for the required deposit were sent promptly. However, medical updates were not communicated with the same urgency. Additionally, I was charged a $35 fee despite the procedure not being performed.

Had the clinic acknowledged the situation, offered an apology, or shown understanding of my concerns, my experience might have been different. Instead, their response focused on justifying actions rather than reflecting on how the experience impacted both patient and client.

I am raising concerns about communication practices, client experience, and perceived lack of empathy during stressful and time-sensitive situations.

Based on these experiences, I have decided not to return to this clinic with my pets. I share this review to accurately reflect my experience and to inform other pet owners as they make their decisions.
